thread:
arjun: Observing a steady increase in SSE disconnects and a lot of partial chunks for na-west since ~09:20 UTC. Customer reports: streams stop producing mid-response, then client reconnects and gets 401s for a minute. Any immediate mitigations?

maya: I see spike in connection resets on proxy-sse-front-3 (500->503 on LB metrics). Errors show ECONNRESET and 'unexpected EOF while reading'. Not seeing CPU/GPU pressure on model hosts though.

kevin: Reproduced locally with a curl streaming client. Steps: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines/rdw-chat-stream/sse?region=na-west\"` — after ~6-10s stream suddenly ends with `event: error\ndata: {\"code\":\"sse_disconnect\",\"message\":\"connection reset\"}`.

elaine: Can you paste the proxy logs? I want to check connection pooling and upstream timeouts.

maya: Proxy tail: ```
proxy-sse-front-3 | 2026-10-11T09:23:12Z DEBUG upstream read error: EOF
proxy-sse-front-3 | 2026-10-11T09:23:12Z WARN connection reset by peer
proxy-sse-front-3 | 2026-10-11T09:23:13Z ERROR 502 writing chunk to client: write tcp 10.0.31.22:443->...: broken pipe
```

arjun: Noticing auth-service complaining about token validation spikes around same time, lots of transient 500s. That explains the 401s after reconnect. Might be cascading: proxy retries reconnect -> hits auth -> gets 5xx -> client auth fails.

kevin: Agreed. I see increased latency to auth-kms (p50 120ms -> 900ms). Could be a KMS throttling/backoff causing validation timeouts.

maya: Immediate mitigations I'm proposing: 1) flip proxy-sse-front cluster to route prefer-secondary region (na-east) for new SSE connects for 10m via routing policy; 2) increase auth-service read timeouts and add token-cached bypass for in-flight reconnects for 5m; 3) deploy temporary rate-limit relaxation for existing long-lived SSE connections to avoid reconnect storms. Thoughts?

kevin: For (1) can we do a canary route so we don't migrate all traffic? Traffic is heavy but still under our dedicated pool. I'd suggest 20% to na-east initially.

elaine: Support ops, notify customers on affected SKUs? We should update status page and set TTL ~30m.

support-ops: Opening incident page and customers list now. Draft status: "Investigating partial SSE disconnections in na-west impacting streaming sessions. Fallback routing and auth mitigations in progress." Will post in 5 min.

sre-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-20261011-NAW-SSE (severity: high). On-call: maya. Runbook link: /runbooks/sse-degradations.

maya: Executed routing change: `rbctl set-route-policy proxy-sse-front prefer-region=na-east weight=20% --scope na-west` — 20% of new connects are going to na-east. Monitoring now.

arjun: Auth-service fix: bumped token cache TTL to 60s and increased validation worker pool by +20% on auth-prod-2. Rolling restart staged.

kevin: Patch applied to proxy to avoid retransmitting partial buffer on reconnect — reduces duplicate partial outputs. Also switching long-poll clients to chunked keepalive headers where possible.

maya: Observability: connection resets down 70% within 6m after changes. However, we're still seeing a subset of clients that reconnect frequently and get 401s for ~30-90s. Looks correlated with a specific token issuer batch.

arjun: Can ops correlate tokens to issuer id? If it's a single issuer we can whitelist or force-local validation for those tokens.

support-ops: Checking logs... issuer_id=acme-payments-service-42 shows 3x higher failure rate. Likely they have a token rotation pattern that's interacting poorly with our caching TTL.

elaine: Short-term: create a policy to accept recent-but-rotated tokens for 2 minutes (grace window) to reduce auth fallout. Also, offer affected customers a temporary credit and an optional route pin to na-east.

kevin: Added temporary grace window config: `auth.config.token_rotation_grace_seconds = 120` — rolled to auth-prod-1/2. Monitoring token validation error rate.

maya: Status update posted at 09:34 UTC: "Mitigations deployed: partial routing to na-east, auth cache TTL adjusted, token grace window enabled. Customer reconnect and 401 errors decreasing. Investigating upstream KMS latency."

arjun: Next steps: 1) deep dive on KMS throttling metrics (tickets with cloud provider), 2) desktop repro guide for support engineering, 3) postmortem owners and timeline.

kevin: Repro guide (add to incident):
1) Start a streaming SSE client: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotate-token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines/rdw-chat-stream/sse?region=na-west"`
2) Send prompt that produces long stream (~20 tokens/sec).
3) Observe mid-stream cut and `event: error` with `sse_disconnect` or `401` after reconnect.
4) Collect proxy logs from host `proxy-sse-front-*` and `auth-prod-*`.

maya: Assigning postmortem: elaine (owner), arjun (SRE ops), kevin (runtime). ETA draft in 48h.

support-ops: Notified top 5 affected customers and offered routing pin + 10% credits.

maya: Closing loop: metrics trending toward baseline, leaving mitigations in place for 1 hour then gradually roll back. If we see >5% reconnects again, we escalate to provider.

kevin: Added a regression alert rule to detect partial-chunk-rate > 0.5% per minute so we can act earlier next time.

arjun: Good work. Save logs and runbook updates to the incident ticket. We'll reconvene after postmortem. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: INC-20261011-NAW-SSE -> mitigations applied, monitoring.
